we describe the functional and compositional differences across EVs and NVEPs, including EVs, exomeres and supermeres, isolated from GBM patient-derived xenograft (PDX) cells and CRC cells based on multi-omics approaches.

To better understand the ontology of EVs, we assessed the protein composition of donor cells and UC-purified 15k and 167k EV fractions for GBM6, GBM39 and GBM59 PDXs using large scale liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS).
Mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) identified 6413 proteins in exomeres and 4983 in supermeres

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The proteomics analysis was performed on isolated extracellular vesicles (15k and 167k EVs) and non-vesicular extracellular nanoparticles (exomeres and supermeres) purified via differential ultracentrifugation. While donor cell extracts were also analyzed for comparison, the primary scope of the proteomics experiment is the extracellular vesicle/nanoparticle proteome.
